item.title: SCP-5302:
item.content:encoded:
It is a good article, but there are some glaring problems.

The Containment makes it clear and all-too-relevant that gravestones and coffins are transplanted from somewhere else to some other place, but the description gives nothing about it. Although the log does include a coffin it doesn't disappear either, so there is no relation whatsoever between the article and its containment procedures (apart from keeping people from entering).

Also it is said that the con artist evaded the Foundation in the past, but stops on that and it doesn't have any impact in the story whatsoever, so it must either be elaborated on or removed, IMHO, 'cause it does stand out.

Some info on the prices at the bar itself would be good, although it already made it clear that it costs actual common money. I would argue for a more thorough investigation on all the things, but it doesn't really need it.

item.title: SCP-3219:
item.content:encoded:
I was first going for no-vote, but coming here and reading the explanations of the author helped me to finish connecting dots in my head. Since the explanation makes sense, I think an upvote is deserved, it really made for an enjoyable reading.

As a matter of fact I won't go for the Reality Bender thing, I find the very definition lame. This child was either a psychopath, deformed or both, and somehow something in the whole situation sparked its connection to the earth, there is no need for a previous anomaly.

The question that remains is how much did the sheriff actually knew of the whole thing. It can be anything from just noticing something going on and avoiding it, all the way up to participating in the original mess and fearing consequences.

item.title: SCP-5762:
item.content:encoded:
Downvote for me, sorry.

The concept is good and its core, the logs, was well done. As a general narrative I have no qualms.

But I think a lot of aspects from the Foundation got lost for no reason:

1- This is not Neutralized, since it still works, it is just depressed;
2- It shouldn't be in a Standard Containment, first because it is an SCP, secondly because it is Sentient and self-motile;
3- The description cuts right to "it Anderson's, so that's why it is anomalous", giving unnecessary context without describing it or it properties in any relevant way. It sounds like a Task Force report, not the finished article;
4- A lot of details on GOIs' activities that have no bearing in the story and I don't really care;
5- They do no test whatsoever, then someone wants to use it because why not.

Let me be clear, I have nothing against the Foundation deciding to use an anomaly whose effects are actually useful and understood enough for some safety and reliability. But without tests there is no safety and reliability in it. This thing is a frigging autonomous AI, it could do horrible shit out of the blue for unknown reasons, at the very least, without some tests.

Some logs could be those tests, by the way, at least some of them. A single dummy test isn't nearly enough, and even downplaying the dumb "lets fry D-Classes for cheap data"a surgeon just begs for tests with D-Classes that needed the surgery because of accidents and stuff.

As a general concept we already have SCP-2295 and, with a different area of work, SCP-1230. So the good parts aren't enough for not downvoting.

item.title: SCP-4877:
item.content:encoded:
I don't know if I get it at all. So many people praising the article, but I really saw nothing so worthwhile to read. To me it was very subpar.

Sincerely I don't think most of the article makes sense. Not because of the narrative, but the way it is written and the decisions made just don't sound like the Foundation to me, simply because they don't sound like professional to me.

Maybe if the article was rearranged just for the investigation to be all Abagail's own and not even found out by the Foundation before its end, then it would work better for me, although even then it would be just an ok article.

But who can argue against more than 200 upvotes? Something here worked for a lot of people. To me it is an easy downvote.

PS.: Well written, though, and I would love to see more simple human behaviour like in this one, this part was really well done.

item.title: SCP-4877:
item.content:encoded:
The experience isn't less corporeal at all.

Olivia went up and, since she probably didn't questioned herself, stayed up to the very end.

Lin went up, met the entity, doubted it and opened her eyes. When she opened her eyes she fell before the very end of the phenomena.

Keep in mind this last log is a video feed recorded in her computer. Lin saw nothing of the description, it was the actual camera. Only after she doubts the entity does she open her eyes and see anything at all. And as it seems, what she sees is something the camera can't get because of the light from behind the entity.

item.title: SCP-5672: Re: thanks for the feedback i guess
item.content:encoded:
Saying stuff like this isn't good. Trying to make an SCP wasn't a bad idea; that's how people get these done, they try. However, a better idea would've been to get feedback on your concept/draft BEFORE posting. People who read finished articles aren't obligated to explain their votes, so it's better to get critique beforehand.

We have a forum channel in the "Forum" section dedicated to giving or getting feedback. I suggest you check it out!
